summary: A 1953 Cal Fire lookout tower on Iron Peak in Mendocino County, replacing a 1926 state lookout; staffed as needed. A directory marks an Iron Peak entry Gone; unresolved.

facts.design: Metal lookout tower built 1953 to replace an earlier 1926 lookout
facts.status_note: NHLR (registered 2016) says Cal Fire staffs the tower as needed; Peakbagging.com has June 2006 photos of it. Neither gives a later condition. A firelookout.org directory list marks an Iron Peak entry (FFLOS US 1892, CA 87) as Gone; it is not tied to either station.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the earlier lookout was 1926. The volunteer history page has a 1927 article about a lookout station built with a road, and the same article appears under both June 3, 1927 and June 3, 1929. Treated as 1926 for the first station; the 1927 and 1929 items are presented as land and road news.

A 1930 item places the station nine miles northeast of Laytonville; a 1935 item says about nine miles northwest. Not resolved; the story uses northeast, which the 1929 bill and the 1930 item both give, and reports the 1935 northwest item as a conflict.

NHLR and Peakbagging.com describe the 1953 tower (photos 2006; registration 2016); firelookout.org marks an Iron Peak entry Gone. The Gone entry may refer to the 1926 station, but no source says so. Story keeps the conflict open.

notes_for_editor: The volunteer page has no entries after 1956, so current staffing and access are unverified; no access key was recorded. The 1927 and 1929 road-and-lookout article is the same text under two dates, so the story does not give it a date of its own. The firelookout.org Gone entry (FFLOS US 1892, CA 87) is unresolved; it may be the former 1926 station. The Rattlesnake Fire (1953, Mendocino National Forest) turned up in search results but is a different incident and was not used.
